definitions.explanation: Luxurious patterned silk woven in the Nishijin district of northwest Kyoto, famous above all for kimono sashes ({帯|おび}). The name is a protected regional brand and stands for the finest traditional Japanese textiles.

examples.japanese: {西陣織|にしじんおり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{帯|おび}→帯：02610_obi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{締|し}める→締める：10057_shimeru⟧。
examples.english: To tie a Nishijin brocade obi.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{西陣織|にしじんおり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{着物|きもの}→着物：01309_kimono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧にして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: My grandmother takes great care of her Nishijin-woven kimono.

examples.japanese: ⟦{京都|きょうと}→京都：09484_kyouto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{工房|こうぼう}→工房：12418_koubou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{職人|しょくにん}→職人：09868_shokunin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{西陣織|にしじんおり}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{手織|てお}り⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{様子|ようす}→様子：01521_yousu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見学|けんがく}→見学：00214_kengaku⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: At a workshop in Kyoto, we watched craftsmen weaving Nishijin brocade by hand.

notes:
Named after {西陣|にしじん}, the Kyoto district where the weavers settled; the name comes from the western army's camp there during the Ōnin War (1467–1477). Woven from dyed threads, so the pattern is part of the cloth rather than printed on it.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {西陣織|にしじんおり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{帯|おび}→帯：02610_obi⟧: a Nishijin obi
- {西陣織|にしじんおり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{着物|きもの}→着物：01309_kimono⟧: a Nishijin kimono
- {西陣織|にしじんおり}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{職人|しょくにん}→職人：09868_shokunin⟧: a Nishijin weaver

CULTURAL NOTE:
One of Japan's best-known ⟦{伝統工芸|でんとうこうげい}→伝統工芸：17478_dentoukougei⟧ (traditional crafts). Together with Kyoto's dyed {友禅|ゆうぜん} silk it represents the high end of kimono culture.
